setup.welcomeBody: This app runs on your computer and only reads your mail. For each email, a short excerpt is sent to TypeSafe's Jev model to classify it. Nothing is moved, deleted or marked as read.
setup.keyStep1: Open the TypeSafe console and sign in.
setup.network: Could not reach the service. Check your connection.
setup.mailAuth: The server rejected the email or app password
setup.howTo: How to create an app password
setup.envMode: Secrets are read from your .env file (Docker mode).
setup.welcomeFact1: Runs on this computer. Your mail and settings stay here.
setup.welcomeFact2: Read-only. Nothing is moved, deleted or marked as read.
setup.welcomeFact3: For each email, the sender, subject, start of the text, link domains and attachment names go to Jev, TypeSafe's model, to be classified.
setup.welcomeNeeds: You'll need a TypeSafe API key and an app password from your mail provider. It takes about five minutes.
setup.keyIntro: The key lets this app call Jev with your own TypeSafe account. Checking it is free.
setup.keySaved: A key is already saved on this computer. Paste a new one only to replace it.
setup.keyStored: Saved in your system keychain, never in the browser.
setup.keyEnvMissing: Add the key to your .env file as TYPESAFE_API_KEY and restart the app. You can check a key here first; it won't be saved.
setup.keyEnvOk: The key works. Add it to your .env file as TYPESAFE_API_KEY and restart the app to continue.
setup.mailIntro: Your provider needs an app password: a separate password just for this app that you can revoke at any time. Your usual password won't work.

gmail.step1: Turn on 2-Step Verification in your Google Account. App passwords only appear once it's on.
gmail.step2: Open App passwords, type a name such as “JEV Mail Filtering” and select Create.
gmail.step3: Copy the 16-character password and paste it below. Google shows it only once.

icloud.step1: Check that two-factor authentication is on for your Apple Account.
icloud.step2: Sign in to your Apple Account, open Sign-In and Security › App-Specific Passwords and create one.
icloud.step3: Paste it below, with your iCloud address (…@icloud.com) as the email.

yahoo.step1: Open Account security in your Yahoo account.
yahoo.step2: Select Generate app password, type a name such as “JEV Mail Filtering” and select Generate.
yahoo.step3: Copy the password and paste it below.

imap.step1: Look up your provider's IMAP server. Most use port 993 with TLS.
imap.step2: If your account uses two-step sign-in, create an app password in its security settings.
imap.step3: Enter the server, your email and the password below.

setup.mailEnvNote: In .env mode the app password comes from IMAP_PASSWORD. Leave this empty to use it.
setup.mailEnvMissing: In .env mode the app password is read from IMAP_PASSWORD, which isn't set. Add it to your .env file and restart; what you type here is only used to test the connection.
setup.hostRequired: Enter the IMAP server, for example imap.example.com.
setup.badRequest: Check the fields and try again.
setup.scopeIntro: Choose what Jev reads on the first run. Later syncs only fetch new mail.
setup.estimateHint: An estimate from the number of emails; the real cost depends on their length. At most {max} emails per sync.
setup.estimateUnavailable: Couldn't estimate the cost right now. You can still start.
setup.syncingBody: Jev is sorting your recent mail. This can take a few minutes; keep this page open. Your mailbox is not changed.
setup.syncNotReady: The analysis couldn't start: the API key or the app password is missing. In .env mode, check TYPESAFE_API_KEY and IMAP_PASSWORD.

settings.title: Settings
settings.thresholdsHelp: Changes apply instantly and never call Jev again.
settings.wipeConfirm: This deletes the local database and stored credentials. Your mailbox is not touched. Continue?
settings.intro: Everything here is stored on this computer.
settings.thresholdsSectionHelp: How sure Jev must be before an email lands in a column.
settings.syncHelp: How often new mail is fetched and analysed while the app is running.
settings.modelHelp: Advanced. The default is the pinned version the published evaluation ran on, so results stay stable. jev-latest always uses the newest Jev, which may classify differently.
settings.modelInvalid: Enter a model name without spaces, for example jev-1.13.0.
settings.reconfigureHelp: Change the mailbox, app password or API key.
settings.dangerHelp: Removes the local database, your settings and the stored credentials. Your mailbox is not touched.
settings.wipeFailed: Couldn't delete the data. Try again.
